heldout_percent.source: owner brief: hold out 10% of synthetic domains for early stopping

declined_floor.source: a kind with few positive decisions still keeps this many declines, so 'none' is never unseen

seed.source: fixed so a corpus converts to the same split and order every time

iters.source: an upper bound (about one pass); the run ends earlier by patience or the time cap

lora_layers.source: mlx-lm's default count of top layers adapted

learning_rate.source: a starting point for a one-token target; the held-out loss curve decides the checkpoint

min_free_disk_gb.source: a run keeps at most the best and the latest adapter plus metrics (well under 1 GB); the owner's start-now order 2026-10-21 replaced the earlier 6 GB brief

noise_decisions.source: a kind regresses when it loses more than this many decisions net of gains; the benches hold 13-96 decisions, where one flip is noise

grad_accumulation.source: owner: batch size 1 with gradient accumulation; 8 one-example steps per update

mlx_memory_limit_gb.source: owner: training is memory-capped so other work keeps running

mlx_cache_limit_gb.source: owner: a small MLX cache; the cache is also cleared every step

footprint_abort_gb.source: owner: abort cleanly past this process footprint

metrics_file.source: owner: the dashboard reads exactly this file

val_batch.source: held-out examples per forward pass during evaluation; all held-out examples are scored each time

patience_evals.source: lead 2026-10-21: stop when held-out loss has not improved for 3 evaluations

max_hours.source: lead 2026-10-21: hard cap of about 3 hours per run

val_sample.source: lead 2026-10-21: a fixed stratified held-out sample (~300, balanced by kind and domain) for the periodic evals and early stopping; the full held-out set is scored once on the best adapter
